title: Column subtraction without regrouping, within 50 to within 1,000,000 (pilot: six SU-C skills)

summary: Pilot family card, scoped to six skills: the no-regrouping rungs of the SU-C ladder (design/catalogue/subtraction.md C4, C6-C9), one stacked problem per boxed cell on the `stack` template with no regroup row. The six differ ONLY in the size of the minuend (within 50, 100, 1,000, 10,000, 100,000, 1,000,000); every other thing that changes is its own step.
teaches: Subtract with the column (standard) algorithm when no column needs regrouping: line the places up, subtract the ones first, then each place to the left. Grades 2-5 (CCSS 2.NBT.B.5, 2.NBT.B.7, 3.NBT.A.2, 4.NBT.B.4; WRM Y2-Y4 column subtraction without exchange). "Within N" bounds the MINUEND (the largest number on the page and the answer's ceiling), never the subtrahend alone.
research: From repo sources (PEDAGOGY_STANDARD L-3, design/catalogue/subtraction.md SU-C ladder and rows 145-160, design/PROBLEM_TYPES.md AS rows, the `stack` card); MW4K/IXL research pending logins (Q-H4).
problemTypes: AS-05 vertical subtract with labelled columns (place heads, answer boxes below the rule, no regroup row) — the core item
AS-11 rewrite a horizontal problem in the grid (alignment, "Do not solve.") — the `sub-setup` page these skills already list
ragged lengths: a shorter subtrahend lined up under the ones (2d − 1d, 3d − 2d, …) as its own section, never mixed at random with equal lengths
zero cases as their own section: a 0 digit in the top number (`n − 0`, `0 − 0`), a column that leaves 0 (`n − n`), an answer with fewer digits than the minuend
AS-15 check a subtraction by adding (`check` line under the stack) — a later step, same drawing
progression: within 50 (`sub_50_no_regroup`): 2-digit − 2-digit, minuend ≤ 50, T O heads, answer boxes, no regroup row (L-3 1-4; SU-C C4)
within 100 (`sub_100_no_regroup`): the same item, minuend ≤ 99 — ONLY the minuend range changes (C4, second half)
the T O heads fade on a dedicated step; the grid and boxes stay (L-3 7)
within 1,000 (`sub_1k_no_regroup`): 3-digit minuend, H T O heads back on; 3d − 2d (ragged) first, then 3d − 3d (C6; catalogue row 151)
zero cases at 3 digits: a 0 in the top number, a column that leaves 0, an answer with fewer digits (one section, not seeded at random into the plain page)
within 10,000 (`sub_10k_no_regroup`): 4 digits, TH H T O heads (C7)
within 100,000 (`sub_100k_no_regroup`): 5 digits, TTh heads, comma in numbers and answer (C8)
within 1,000,000 (`sub_1m_no_regroup`): 6 digits, HTh heads (C9); then check by adding (AS-15) on any size

drawing.sizes: digits 16 / 22 / 28 pt; writing height Hw 6 / 8 / 10 mm; answer row 8 / 10 / 12 mm; heads row 4 / 5 / 6 mm; regroup row 6 / 7 / 8 mm; carry box 5 / 6 / 7 mm; subtraction headroom 8 / 10 / 12 mm (`js/modules/sheet/tokens.js` SIZES). Tracks 0.72 em plain, 0.95 em with any regroup scaffold (TY-20, TY-21); default size L. The answer row has as many boxes as the minuend has digits (the widest answer the section can reach, never the item's own answer length).
notes: Payload (`q.cell = {template: 'stack', v: 1, payload}`): `operands: [a, b]`, `op: '-'`, `ans`, `regroup: false`, `heads` (from the support level), `answer: 'boxes'`, `ansDigits` = digits of the band's largest minuend. The scaffold ladder decides heads and answer boxes, never the generator (SCC-Q10).
No regroup row and no subtraction headroom on these skills: the name promises no regrouping, so the strip would be an empty prompt (catalogue: the legacy cell already hides it on `_no_regroup`).
States blank / traced / answered / wrong share one geometry (SCC-T10). Key: answer digits only, leading answer boxes left blank (AK-1, INK-31).
Screen: one input per answer box in the printed geometry, ones box focused first, typing right to left (SCC-T15).

ownerRulings.ruling: "Within N" bounds the ANSWER (for subtraction: the minuend), never the operands.
Pupil-facing text says "regroup", never "borrow" (P-32); the legacy column caption "Use top row for borrowing" goes.
Writing boxes are slightly rounded (SL-11); a row of digit boxes is ONE outline with dividers (SL-12).
Key answers print reddish orange, keys only (INK-31).
SPEC, NOT BUILT: on screen the regroup boxes an item NEEDS are required and marked. A no-regroup item needs none, so these six skills show no regroup boxes on any host; paper unchanged.
SPEC, NOT BUILT: `carry: top | bottom` is addition and × only; subtraction stays at the top. It does not apply to these skills.
A distinct option (new size class, new task kind) is also a findable preset skill; small tweaks stay plain options.

The ladder in O-rubric terms: O2 number size = the six skills themselves (within N, minuend-bounded); O3 support = place heads (hint, fades on its step), answer boxes and grid (structural, stay); O6 stacked / across (across belongs to the `sub-setup` rewrite page).

Proposed (section 9): `lengths: same | shorter` (ragged as its own section), `zeros: on | off` (zero-case section), `heads: on | off` via the support level. Each is a plain option, not a preset skill, except where section 9 says a new skill (`sub_2d_1d`, catalogue C3).

openQuestions.q: Shared defects D1, D2, D5 (legacy pink / orange column visual, "borrowing" caption, place heads missing below grade 3 and above 3 digits): patch the legacy `column-sub` cell or move the six onto `stack`?
openQuestions.recommended: Move all six onto `stack` (`q.cell`, `regroup: false`) in one change and stop emitting `buildColumnVisual` for them; heads then come from the support level at every size (T O … HTh), which closes D1, D2 and D5 together. No new legacy handler (CLAUDE.md: do not extend the legacy path).

openQuestions.q: D3 (`minVal = maxVal/10`): what number band does each size deal, given "within N" bounds the minuend?
openQuestions.recommended: The minuend runs over the size's own digit count up to N (within 50: 21-50; within 100: 51-99, since 100 − n always regroups; within 1,000: 100-999; and so on to 999,999), the subtrahend is any number whose every digit is ≤ the digit above it, and the answer may be small (47 − 42 = 5). Sizes below a band belong to the skill below, so each rung adds one thing: a longer minuend.

openQuestions.q: D3 / D4 (ragged lengths arrive at random): how do shorter subtrahends enter?
openQuestions.recommended: As their own section, never at random: a plain option `lengths: same | shorter` (default `same`); at 3 digits and up the Lesson/Guided order is `shorter` first, then `same` (catalogue row 151 research). 2d − 1d is a distinct skill, the NEW `sub_2d_1d` preset (catalogue C3), so it is not an option on `sub_50_no_regroup`.

openQuestions.q: Zero handling (`n − 0`, `0 − 0`, `n − n` = 0, an answer with fewer digits): seed it into every page or give it its own section?
openQuestions.recommended: Its own section from 3 digits up (plain option `zeros: on | off`, default off on the plain page; P-1 one new thing). Within 50 / 100 may deal a 0 ones digit naturally (40 − 20) but never seeds it. The key leaves leading answer boxes blank; the pupil is never asked to write a leading 0.

openQuestions.q: Answer slot shape: how many boxes, and does the box count leak the answer length?
openQuestions.recommended: One outline with dividers (SL-12), as many boxes as the band's largest minuend has digits, the same on every item of the section; never the item's own answer length (that would give away "the answer has 1 digit"). Commas print in the minuend and subtrahend from 5 digits up and sit in a narrow fixed gap in the answer row, not in a box.

openQuestions.q: D6 (six digits at 2 columns is tight): shrink, or fewer columns?
openQuestions.recommended: Never shrink (SCC-T4): the capacity rows decide. At L, 5- and 6-digit items take 1 column if the two-column cell is narrower than the stack plus gutter; at S / M they keep 2. The capacity check is a gate number, not a judgement.

openQuestions.q: SU-M1 (smaller from larger) is invisible on a no-regroup page. Seed regroup non-examples here (P-10)?
openQuestions.recommended: No: the skill's name promises no regrouping and `ws-content-audit` holds it to that. The non-examples and the decide page live on the `_mixed` skills (SU-R R2). Here the key's `wrongAnswer` is built from SU-M7 (adds), M-ALIGN (left-lined) and M-ZERO, which do show on these items.

openQuestions.q: MW4K / IXL research is pending logins (Q-H4). Sign now?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes, sign now; add the research to section 2 when the logins work, and re-sign only if the problem types or progression change.
